clue.text: Drop in crucial point in conflict

indicators.note: in means the word for drop is placed inside the word for crucial

parts.note: crucial, as in a dire need, gives DIRE
to drop or sink in the middle is to sag
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dip at the critical moment of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop in' looks like a phrase meaning pay a visit, but the two words split: one is the sinking, the other the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To conflict, said of opinions or accounts, is to be at odds or differ, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Australian monster rabbit, gutted, very cheap

indicators.note: gutted means an inner letter of the pet word is taken out of its middle

parts.note: a bunny is a child's word for a rabbit
1p, one penny, is very cheap, read as the letters I and P

explanation.surface: An outback beast is a disembowelled rabbit sold for next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 of 1p (one penny, the smallest British coin) is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The bunyip is a creature of Aboriginal Australian folklore said to lurk in swamps and billabongs.

clue.text: Shining with desire: ours is amazing

parts.note: lust is strong desire

indicators.note: amazing in its old sense of bewildered or confused signals that the letters of ours get jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone glowing with longing declares what the two of them share is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is amazing' is the anagram signal, using amaze in its old sense of bewilder.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustrous describes something with a sheen or gloss, gleaming and bright like polished silk.

clue.text: By being executed, prophet died

indicators.note: being executed means losing the head, so the first letter of the prophet's name goes

parts.note: Nathan is the Old Testament prophet who rebuked King David

explanation.surface: A grim tale: nearby, a prophet is put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: Beheading NATHAN leaves ATHAN, then D is added.
explanation.definitionFit: By can mean near or beside, and something close within reach is nearby, so the two phrases are interchangeable.

clue.text: City announced part of coastal path

indicators.note: announced means the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a bay is part of a coast and a route is a path, so the phrase gives bay route

explanation.surface: A city is proclaimed to be a stretch of seaside walkway.
explanation.walkthrough: BAY ROUTE spoken sounds like the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital of Lebanon, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: To jeer at items performed upset stars

parts.note: to boo is to jeer at a performer

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a set is the list of items a band or comedian performs

explanation.surface: An audience jeering at an act unsettles the star performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the band's programme upside down, as befits a down clue; 'stars' means a constellation, not celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootes, the Herdsman, is a northern constellation containing the bright star Arcturus.

clue.text: Complain of a foreign parent

definitions.meaning: to grumble or grouse under one's breath

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a mother or father from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters are an English verb and German for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbling under one's breath is a mild form of complaint; in German the word is the noun for mother.

clue.text: Swiftly advances strategies to snare husband

indicators.note: to snare means to catch and hold, so the strategies word traps the husband letter inside it

parts.note: ruses are crafty strategies or tricks

explanation.surface: A schemer moves quickly, with plans to trap a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to snare' puts H inside RUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To rush is to move forward hastily, so swiftly advances is the third-person verb.

clue.text: One metre down, plant foolish hoax

indicators.note: foolish suggests letters arranged in silly disorder

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Instructions for burying a fake: a metre deep, put in a silly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolish' rearranges I, M, DOWN and PLANT into the eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Piltdown Man was a famous forgery of fossil remains, unveiled in 1912 and exposed as fake in 1953.

clue.text: Emma, born with appropriate gland

parts.note: an ovary is a gland, appropriate for a woman such as Emma

explanation.surface: A woman named Emma is born with a fitting part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma is not a generic name but Flaubert's heroine, Madame Bovary.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is the first name of the heroine of Flaubert's novel Madame Bovary.

clue.text: I don't believe host is at party

indicators.note: party suggests the letters gathering and mixing as at a social do

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts that the host is at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' rearranges HOST IS AT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a sceptical reply expressing disbelief, much like saying 'really?'

clue.text: Supposed political project at advanced stage taking in English

indicators.note: taking in means the stage word holds the English letter inside it

parts.note: far, as in far gone or far along, means at an advanced stage

explanation.surface: A political scheme is well under way and includes England.
explanation.walkthrough: Project Fear was the label Brexit campaigners gave to the Remain campaign's warnings in 2016; 'Supposed' signals the name was a jibe.
explanation.definitionFit: Opponents dubbed Remain's economic warnings 'Project Fear', so the word completes that alleged campaign's name.

clue.text: Snack, not bad, fed to dogs

indicators.note: fed to means the scrambled word goes into the dogs word, as food goes into a dog

parts.note: poodles are a breed of dog

indicators.note: bad indicates the letters of not are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A snack that's not bad is given to the dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' scrambles the little word and 'fed to' slips it into the dogs just after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot Noodle is a British brand of instant noodles in a plastic pot, a quick and cheap snack.

clue.text: Easing unusual burden carried in ferry trip

indicators.note: carried in means the burden word is held inside the jumbled letters
unusual signals the letters of easing are put in an odd order

parts.note: a cross is a burden to bear, as in 'a cross to bear'

explanation.surface: Easing an unusual load carried on board a ferry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' scrambles the first word and 'carried in' sets the burden in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing the sea by boat is exactly what a ferry trip involves.

clue.text: Showing 11, caught what may be in one's ears

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

parts.words: what may be in one's ears
parts.note: ringing may be heard in one's ears, as with tinnitus

explanation.surface: A sufferer from tinnitus admits to being caught out by what's in their ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to the answer to 11 across, so the definition means showing dread.
explanation.definitionFit: Cringing is shrinking back or cowering, the outward sign of being afraid.

clue.text: Hanged man whose eye is number one

definitions.meaning: an Australian bushranger executed in Melbourne in 1880
in bingo, 'Kelly's eye' is the call for number one

explanation.surface: A man was executed, and his eye was the best.
explanation.walkthrough: Bingo callers give each number a nickname; 'Kelly's eye' is number one.
explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw famous for his home-made armour was hanged, and his surname appears in the bingo call for one.

clue.text: Dangerous situation traps soldiers in great numbers

indicators.note: in means the soldiers sit inside the word for great numbers

parts.note: a mass is a great number of people or things
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A dangerous situation traps large numbers of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A morass is a bog, and figuratively a complicated situation one gets stuck in, a perilous mess.

clue.text: Man enters top command

indicators.note: enters means the man word goes into the word for top

parts.note: best means top or finest
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man comes in carrying the highest order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' signals the insertion; 'Man' at the start of the clue hides its role.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is an order or instruction, as in 'at the king's behest'.

clue.text: Meat typically offered in mess

definitions.meaning: the meal put down for a pet hound, typically meat

explanation.surface: Meat is what's usually served in the soldiers' dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like a military canteen but is the second definition, a shambles.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom for a botched or untidy job is this phrase; literally it is food for a pet.

clue.text: Military account some units forward in the wrong direction

parts.note: SI, the International System, is a set of units of measurement

indicators.note: in the wrong direction means the word for forward is read backwards, upwards in this down clue

parts.note: pert means cheeky or forward

explanation.surface: A report from the front says some units have advanced the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' looks like a direction of travel but means cheeky; 'in the wrong direction' turns PERT into TREP.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitrep, short for situation report, is a military update on the current state of operations.

clue.text: Persian poet sounds affected by cold

indicators.note: sounds means the poet's name is spoken, giving a word pronounced the same

parts.note: Rumi was the thirteenth-century Persian mystic poet

explanation.surface: A Persian poet's voice is husky with a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: RUMI said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumy describes watery, runny eyes or nose, typical symptoms of a cold.

clue.text: Proper time for a little music

parts.note: due means proper or fitting, as in due respect

explanation.surface: It's the right moment for a short tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece for two performers is a short musical composition, here loosely a bit of music.

clue.text: Method, say, in which to obtain backing for an artist

indicators.note: in which means the backwards word goes inside the spoken one
say means the word for method is pronounced, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: manner means method or way

indicators.note: backing means the word for obtain is written in reverse

parts.note: to get is to obtain

explanation.surface: Instructions on a method for getting support for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals the homophone and 'backing' the reversal; 'in which' places the reversed word in the middle of the sound-alike food from heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Mantegna was an Italian Renaissance painter, known for 'The Lamentation over the Dead Christ'.

clue.text: French pupil's name and number

parts.note: eleve is French for a pupil; the 's stands for has, linking to the name

explanation.surface: A French schoolchild's name and number are recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven is a cardinal number, one more than ten.

clue.text: Girl is turning brown

indicators.note: turning means the girl's name and is are read backwards together

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is becoming tanned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses ANNE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment, a yellowish or reddish brown colour.

clue.text: An obstinate type last to manifest charm

parts.note: an gives the article A
a mule is a byword for stubbornness

indicators.note: last to means only the final letter of manifest is taken

explanation.surface: A stubborn person finally shows some charm.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a protective charm or talisman worn against evil.
